title: When Roles Fail: Epistemic Constraints on Advocate Role Fidelity in LLM-Based Political Statement Analysis

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring role fidelity (using metrics like Expected Drift Distance and Directional Drift Index) against fact-check results to identify when models abandon assigned advocate roles in favor of their factual training priors (identified as 'Epistemic Role Override').

Comparing role drift metrics across different categories of political statements (economic/social policy, contested empirical claims, and ideologically charged positions) to detect the influence of normative and ideological model priors on role adherence.

Evaluating and comparing role fidelity across English (U.S.-centric) and German political statements to expose regional and language-specific model priors (e.g., observing Mistral's alignment with European policy contexts versus Claude's behavior on U.S. topics).
